## 1. Learning objectives

- Connect to and navigate MySQL and PostgreSQL; translate a SQLite schema with appropriate types
- Modify columns (MODIFY) and write stored procedures with parameters (MySQL)
- Compare vertical/horizontal scaling, replication models (sync/async, read replicas) and sharding
- Grant least-privilege access; demonstrate SQL injection and defend with prepared statements

## 6. Common mistakes

- **C5.1**: using SQLite's double quotes for MySQL identifiers (MySQL uses backticks)
- **C5.2**: FLOAT for money; DECIMAL(M,D) misread (errata #7)
- **C5.3**: omitting existing ENUM values or NOT NULL in the new definition
- **C5.4**: forgetting to change the delimiter; selling an already-sold item twice
- **C5.5**: expecting MySQL-style inline ENUM
- **C5.6**: async replication's data-loss risk; shard hotspots; single point of failure
- **C5.7**: `GRANT ALL ON *.*` in production
- **C5.8**: building SQL with string formatting (Python f-strings, L2138-2147)
